messages:
Maya: Heads-up: int8 onboard canary for seabird-v2 shows a spike in funcall parse failures after the KV-cache + batching tweak. Posting samples and quick notes.
canary-bot: Canary run 2026-03-21T12:34Z finished — parse_fail_rate=2.7% (+2.5pp vs baseline).
Jordan: Thanks. Any example outputs we can inspect?
Maya: Yes — here's a representative failed output we captured (shows up only on int8 + kvbatch>4 + retry).
Maya: ```
Model output:
{"action":"call_tool","name":"lookup","args":{"query":"What's the fastest flight to BOS?",}}
```
Ravi: That trailing comma after the query is invalid JSON. Does it ever appear in fp16 runs?
Maya: No, fp16 and baseline quant runs are clean. This exact trailing comma pattern only on int8 canary traces and when retry/backoff happened.
Sofia: Could be streaming chunk boundary / split token issue — maybe a comma token was emitted as separate final token and the stream reconcat put a comma after closing brace.
Jordan: Do we have token-level logs for a failed trace (tokens + positions)?
infra-bot: Replay job queued for trace id seafowl-9832, token-dump attach will be enabled for that replay.
Maya: Hypothesis: KV-prefix caching + continuous batching under int8 shifts the tokenization boundary so a trailing comma token gets emitted after the object close. When the retry merges chunks it ends up with ",}}" or ",]" in some cases.
Ravi: Sounds plausible. Quick mitigation options: 1) post-gen sanitizer that strips trailing commas and attempts JSON repair; 2) lower kvbatch or disable prefix caching for int8; 3) increase conservative retry spacing so chunk merges are less likely.
Jordan: If we add a sanitizer, make sure we track corrections vs semantic changes — we don't want to silently rewrite user intent. Add a checksum of original text vs sanitized parse.
Maya: Plan: run A/B of sanitizer (regex-based repair + json5 parse fallback) on 100k canary requests, enable token-level dumps for 1% of int8 traffic, and try kvbatch=2 for a small slice. I'll post results by EOD tomorrow.
Sofia: Also add a quick unit in the parser to reject obviously repaired outputs if they change more than a small fraction of characters; metric to watch.
infra-bot: Action items logged: maya -> run-ab(100k with sanitizer); infra -> enable token-dumps(1% int8); eng-ml -> create sanitizer PR and add diff metric.
canary-bot: Noted. Rolling window alert threshold set to 1% parse_fail_rate for now — will trigger if sustained. :rotating_light: 
Jordan: Thanks — let us know if repair reduces parse_fail_rate or we need to roll back the batching tweak. :thumbsup:
